generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy where the disordered chemical environment promotes longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs) that suppress the net magnetic moment and orbital angular momentum, resulting in low coercivity ($H_c$ < 100 Oe) and a magnetic ground state dominated by itinerant electron behavior.
generation.intervention: Controlled thermomechanical processing (e.g., annealing) of the Ti-containing FCC HEA to induce the nucleation of a coherent, chemically ordered BCC (B2) secondary phase with a specific lattice mismatch relative to the FCC matrix, creating localized strain fields without causing bulk phase segregation or loss of the FCC matrix integrity.
generation.conditions: Operating temperatures significantly above room temperature (e.g., 400–600 °C) where the FCC matrix must remain thermodynamically stable against kinetic segregation (as observed in single-phase systems) and the secondary B2 phase must maintain structural coherence to transmit strain.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherent interfaces between the FCC matrix and the B2 secondary phase, which generate localized elastic strain fields that modify the local density of states and suppress the magnitude of longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs) in the adjacent FCC atoms.
generation.mechanism: The local strain fields at the coherent interface lift the degeneracy of the 3d orbitals and reduce the amplitude of LSFs (Longitudinal Spin Fluctuations) in the FCC matrix. As LSFs are responsible for the temperature-dependent suppression of magnetic moments in HEAs, their reduction stabilizes a higher local magnetic moment and restores the orbital angular momentum ($L$), which directly increases the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant ($K_u$) and thus the coercive field ($H_c$).
